title: Correlating Defects in Electroluminescence Images to Photovoltaic Module Power Loss Using DeepLabV3 for Semantic Segmentation
mechanism: Segment every cell of fielded modules with a multi-class EL model and regress module electrical parameters on per-module defect fractions.
adaptation: CSIR (our CSIR source, BenchmarkEL author) shows the class set links to module fill factor. Benchmark severity track: per-module class fractions vs FF / Pmpp, if CSIR shares the electrical data (needs user OK).
min_experiment: No training arm; for the benchmark, request the 680-module EL + IV data and report correlation of predicted inactive / crack fractions with FF and Pmpp.
evidence: R: 680 modules, 48,960 cells, 29 classes after adding 24 brightening samples; brightening fraction explains 42% of FF variance (r2 0.42).

alt_notes.adaptation: Same CSIR lab as our CSIR source: template for a severity post-evaluation (predicted inactive fraction per module v measured power); ask the authors for the paired EL + I-V data.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Severity item only: correlate house inactive fraction with module power if paired data is obtained.

alt_notes.adaptation: Template for the severity step: aggregate our class fractions per module and regress on fill factor or Pmax where CSIR or WattCycle electrical data exist.
alt_notes.min_experiment: If electrical data exist for any of our modules: regress module crack length, inactive fraction on FF; report r2 with module-level CV. No score kill line.

alt_notes.adaptation: Same lab, class scheme and CSIR source as our data and E1. If Pratt shares the 680-module EL + I-V, it becomes the benchmark's power track on the E1-like domain: score each segmenter by how well its per-module inactive / crack / brightening fractions explain FF and Pmpp loss.
